doc.title: Laurena Diggs and Carrie Boote Interview, 1960-09-03

title: Carrie Boote's minstrel show singing: Alexander, Dying Rag, Dollar Bill
summary: Boote as a girl sang in minstrel shows; she recalls fragments of Alexander, Dying Rag and Dollar Bill.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: Let's bother Miss Boots for a while now. Huh? Let's bother Miss Boots for a while now.

Miss Boots, she's a little girl. She'd be on stage singing. Alexander, I'll hear you say you're going away. I'm coming back someday. Sorry to tell you, Alexander. That's what Miss Boots was playing with.
That was a minstrel show we used to have. They called them minstrel shows then, you know. So I used to try to be an actress there. Mm-hmm.
What would you sing, Tiara?
Oh, well, I hated quite a few things I sang. Huh? Actually, it was quite a few things we used to sing, but I never heard them song before and

since. That's the truth. But they must have meant. I heard you say, Alexander, I heard you say you're going away, coming back. Sorry to hear you, Alexander. You should come running back someday. That's what Tiara used to sing on the stage. That's what Tiara used to sing. Yeah. And would be dancing like that. And the arts. You would pull it. Yeah. And all the day.
Well, all right. Let him.
Well, we'll get her to sing Dying Rag for us.
And those songs I never heard, but, you know, I don't know who composed them or what, but we were singing them then.

Well, Dollar Bill is pretty famous, you know. They still making records of that, but if you got a hunt for them, you know. Yeah. But that's still popular. How did Dying Rag go now? I wanted to get that as much as you could remember.
It says, honey, I'm sinking fast. Soon I will breathe my legs. Pever is very high. Doctor say I will die. I'm no longer something. Then I know it's a...
Listen.

I forgot how it went. No, I didn't know. Oh, my honey dear. I must be going to fear. I feel the... See? Stealing something in here. I can't get it together now, but it was... At the end, they said that's the Dying Rag.
I can't think of it. What about Dollar Bill? Do you remember any of that?
What was that? Now they say...
The man's name, Dollar Bill.

No. This song was about whenever you get lucky, and all things come your way. Hold on to every dollar, no matter what the people say. I know just what I'm saying. I've been all around the world, and the only friend that I have had was a good old Dollar Bill. If a friend say, Bill, let's have some wine, tell him no. If a friend say, Bill, let's have a good time, tell him no. Oh. And that's always I can go on that. Now that's a song I never heard, but we sang that in his minstrel shows. They might have been just made up, you know.
Mm-hmm.
And, um... Toot your horn, toot your horn. Yeah. Toot my... Toot your horn something, because I'm in a fog or something like that. Those are all those songs that, you know, that...
Yeah, I can't think of them all now,
because there's so many songs.
